keyTakeaways: Plan Halloween night in four blocks: 5–7 pm doorstep, 7–9 pm dinner, 9–11 pm late, 11 pm–midnight send.
The riskiest hours are early: UK data shows child road casualties rise 17:00–18:59 on Halloween, and CDC counted a fourfold rise in US child pedestrian deaths between 4 and 10 pm.
Joel Best found no substantiated case of a child killed or seriously injured by a contaminated trick-or-treat sweet; check for allergens and choking risks instead.
Peanut-induced anaphylaxis in Canadian children ran at 1.86 times the usual rate on Halloween, which is what the teal pumpkin bowl is for.
A midnight message will likely be read on a phone: 48.3% of SubhSandesh pages are opened on one (platform-wide, not Halloween data).

faqs.question: What time does Halloween night start and finish?
faqs.answer: There is no official time. A CDC analysis of US crash data used 4 to 10 pm because that is when most outdoor Halloween activity among 5- to 14-year-olds happens. Most doorsteps are busiest from dusk to about 8 pm, and many hosts switch the porch light off around 8:30.

faqs.question: What can I do on Halloween night by myself?
faqs.answer: Pick one quiet block, usually 9 to 11 pm: an audio horror drama, a classic public-domain horror story read start to finish, or a solo late screening. End with a letter to yourself to open next 31 October.

faqs.question: What should I do on Halloween if I don't celebrate it?
faqs.answer: Leave a short polite note on the door by 5 pm so children skip your house, then keep the evening your own. Some people light a candle for someone they have lost, since All Saints' Day is 1 November and Día de los Muertos is 1 to 2 November.

faqs.question: Is it rude to turn my porch light off on Halloween?
faqs.answer: No. A dark porch is widely read as a sign that a house is not handing out sweets, and a note on the door makes it clearer still. If you have been handing out, switching off around 8:30 pm is a polite way to close.

faqs.question: What do I do with young kids after trick-or-treating?
faqs.answer: Come home by about 6:30 pm, sort the haul on the kitchen table, check wrappers and allergen labels, and pick two pieces to eat tonight. Then bath, pyjamas and a gentle story so they are asleep by 8.

faqs.question: Do I really need to check my child's Halloween candy?
faqs.answer: Yes, but for the right reasons. Sociologist Joel Best has found no substantiated case of a child killed or seriously injured by a contaminated treat from trick-or-treating, so check for choking-size pieces, open or homemade wrappers from strangers, and allergens instead of poison.

faqs.question: What does a teal pumpkin on a doorstep mean?
faqs.answer: It means the house offers non-food treats, such as stickers or glow bracelets, for children with food allergies. FARE adopted the Teal Pumpkin Project nationally in 2014 and asks hosts to keep those treats in a separate bowl.

faqs.question: What can teenagers do on Halloween night instead of trick-or-treating?
faqs.answer: Lead a younger sibling's route from 5 pm, go on a group costume photo walk with a check-in text, shoot a one-minute horror short on a phone, or hold a sleepover with a pickup time agreed in advance.

faqs.question: How can I celebrate Halloween if I'm working that night?
faqs.answer: Bring a bowl of fun-size sweets for the break room, wear one costume accessory your dress code allows, and write a message on an early break that is set to open at midnight.

faqs.question: What should I send someone at midnight on Halloween?
faqs.answer: Send one personal message rather than a group post. SubhSandesh's /happy-halloween card lets them knock on a little haunted house, carve a pumpkin and read your letter, and the premium version can stay locked behind a countdown until the time you choose.

# Things to Do on Halloween Night: A 5 pm to Midnight Plan

The best things to do on Halloween night depend on which two hours you have: 5 to 7 pm belongs to small children and the front door, 7 to 9 pm to dinners and teenagers, 9 to 11 pm to friends, and the last hour to a quiet message. Below are 28 ideas sorted by who you are, each with a time slot, an estimated cost and indoor or outdoor.

If your night ends with a midnight message, plan for a phone: 48.3% of the pages people make on SubhSandesh are opened on one. People also leave these things late: on Raksha Bandhan 2026, a different festival and a small sample of 89 pages, 49.4% were built on the day itself.

Costs are our US-dollar estimates. Safety numbers come from CDC and UK crash data.

## The 5 pm to midnight template, in four blocks

Halloween is 31 October every year, a Saturday in 2026 and a Sunday in 2027. The night runs in four blocks, and the first is the riskiest outdoors.

- **5–7 pm, the doorstep block.** Small children trick-or-treat. UK crash data shows child road casualties rise between 17:00 and 18:59.
- **7–9 pm, the dinner block.** Sweets get sorted, teenagers head out, couples eat.
- **9–11 pm, the late block.** Parties and pubs; the door goes quiet.
- **11 pm–midnight, the send block.** Check everyone is home; send one message.

## 28 things to do on Halloween night, by who you are

Each idea carries a time slot, estimated cost and indoor or outdoor. Couples get two lines, because date nights have their own guides.

### 1. Solo, including an introvert's night in

A night alone can be a choice, not a gap. These keep it deliberate.

- **Radio-horror hour** (9–10 pm · est. $0 · indoor): *The War of the Worlds* first aired on 30 October 1938.
- **One classic horror story, start to finish** (10–11 pm · est. $0 · indoor): Poe is public domain and short.
- **A late screening, alone** (8–10 pm · est. $10–18 · out): single seats are easy to find.
- **A letter to next year's you** (11–11:30 pm · est. $0 · indoor): open it next 31 October.

### 2. Families with young kids

Aim for an early loop and home by bedtime. Work back from 8 pm lights-out.

- **Visibility check** (4:45 pm · est. $5–10 · indoor): reflective tape, torches, face paint not masks.
- **The early-light loop** (5–6:30 pm · est. $0 · outdoor): one street and back, crossing only at corners.
- **Kitchen-table candy sort** (6:45–7:15 pm · est. $0 · indoor): check wrappers, keep two pieces for tonight.
- **Bath, pyjamas, one gentle story** (7:30–8 pm · est. $0 · indoor): end on something cosy.

### 3. Teens

Teens want independence; parents want a check-in. These give both.

- **Lead a younger sibling's route** (5–6:30 pm · est. $0 · outdoor): torch-bearer, paid in first pick.
- **Group costume photo walk** (7–8:30 pm · est. $0 · outdoor): three or more, one street, a text home at 8:30.
- **A 60-second horror short on a phone** (8:30–10 pm · est. $0 · indoor or outdoor): one jump scare, edited.
- **Sleepover with an agreed pickup time** (10 pm–late · est. $10–20 · indoor): films agreed by age rating.

### 4. Friends

Friends own the late block. Book ticketed things early: Halloween is a weekend night in 2026 and 2027.

- **Horror-themed escape room** (7–8:30 pm · est. $25–40 a person · indoor): a fixed end time.
- **Halloween karaoke** (9–11 pm · est. $10–25 a person · indoor): *Monster Mash* and *Thriller* are compulsory.
- **Costume pub crawl** (9 pm–midnight · est. $30–60 a person · out): three stops, ride home booked first.
- **Late diner debrief** (11 pm–midnight · est. $10–15 a person · indoor): rank the outfits over pancakes.

### 5. Couples

Our Halloween date guides cover date nights in depth. These two suit the night itself.

- **Costume dinner booked for 7 pm** (7–9 pm · est. $40–100 · indoor): ahead of the party crowd.
- **The midnight swap** (11:45 pm–midnight · est. $0 · indoor): one message each, landing at 12.

### 6. The candy host at the door

Your night is 5 to 8 pm, outdoors. Make it easy and visible.

- **Doorstep station** (5–8 pm · est. $20–40 in sweets · outdoor): bowl at the path's end, so nobody climbs dark steps.
- **A teal pumpkin bowl** (5–8 pm · est. $10–15 · outdoor): stickers or glow bracelets in a separate bowl. More below.
- **Costume tally** (5–8 pm · est. $0 · outdoor): witches versus skeletons, posted to your street's chat.
- **Porch light off** (8:30 pm · est. $0 · indoor): a dark porch says you are done.

### 7. Working the night shift or stuck at work

Ten minutes of a break is enough. None of these breaks a uniform rule.

- **Shared treat bowl** (start of shift · est. $10 · indoor): fun-size sweets in the break room.
- **One costume accessory** (all shift · est. $5 · indoor): cat ears or a pumpkin badge.
- **A message scheduled for midnight** (any break · est. $0 · indoor): written at 7 pm, opened at 12.

### 8. Not celebrating, but marking the night quietly

Opting out is fine. These mark the evening without joining in.

- **Polite note on the door** (5 pm · est. $0 · indoor): "No sweets tonight, happy Halloween."
- **A candle for someone you have lost** (9–9:30 pm · est. $3 · indoor): All Saints' Day is 1 November and Día de los Muertos 1–2 November.
- **An early, offline night** (9 pm onwards · est. $0 · indoor): do not disturb on.

## Which 2-hour block suits you?

This table groups the eight sections into five rows by best block and estimated cost. It is a planning start, not a quote.

| Who you are | Best 2-hour block | Est. cost | Indoor or outdoor |
|---|---|---|---|
| Families with children under 9 | 5–7 pm | $5–15 | Outdoor, then indoor |
| Candy host or night shift | 5–7 pm | $10–40 | Doorstep or workplace |
| Teens or couples | 7–9 pm | $0–20 teens; $40–100 couples | Outdoor for teens, indoor for couples |
| Friends | 9–11 pm | $10–60 a person | Indoor or out |
| Solo, introvert or not celebrating | 9–11 pm | $0–18 | Indoor |

The cheapest nights are the quiet ones. Most outdoor time sits in the first block, the riskiest on the roads.

## If it rains on 31 October: 5 plan-B swaps

Rain hits the outdoor 5 to 7 pm block hardest. Each swap keeps the slot and moves inside.

- **Indoor trick-or-treat** (5–6 pm · est. $5): each room becomes a door.
- **Shorter loop, umbrellas, no masks** (5–5:45 pm · est. $0): wet masks slip.
- **Doorstep moves to the hall** (5–8 pm · est. $0): bowl inside the open door.
- **Photo walk becomes a home photoshoot** (7–8:30 pm · est. $0): one lamp, one sheet.
- **Crawl becomes one venue** (9 pm–midnight · est. $20–40 a person): pick one and stay.

## Halloween night safety: the 5–7 pm road risk, candy checks and the teal pumpkin

The real Halloween hazard is traffic, not sweets. A [CDC report on 1975–1996 US crash data](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/preview/mmwrhtml/00049687.htm) counted 89 pedestrian deaths among 5- to 14-year-olds between 4 and 10 pm on 31 October, about four a year against one on other evenings. It named midblock crossing, dark costumes and masks as risks and urged constant adult supervision.

Britain shows the same window. [Hsu and colleagues' 2021 study of 73,587 child road casualties, 1990–2017](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC8430693), found more casualties between 17:00 and 18:59 on Halloween than on other days, and 34.2% higher odds of death or serious injury between 17:00 and 17:59.

Poisoned sweets are mostly legend. Sociologist [Joel Best, who has tracked Halloween sadism reports since a 1985 study of four US newspapers](https://www.joelbest.net/halloween-sadism), writes that he has been "unable to find a substantiated report of a child being killed or seriously injured by a contaminated treat picked up in the course of trick-or-treating." The infamous 1974 Texas cyanide death was a father poisoning his own son.

So check for real dangers: bin anything unwrapped or homemade from strangers, remove choking-size pieces for under-5s, read allergen labels. Best notes hospital X-rays cannot detect drugs or poisons anyway.

Allergy is the bigger candy risk. In [a Canadian study of 1,390 child anaphylaxis cases from 2011 to 2020](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC7532006), peanut-induced anaphylaxis on Halloween ran at 1.86 times the rate of the rest of the year. The [Teal Pumpkin Project from FARE](https://www.foodallergy.org/our-initiatives/awareness-campaigns/living-teal/teal-pumpkin-project), adopted nationally in 2014, asks hosts to offer non-food treats in a separate bowl.

## The midnight send: a Halloween card for one person

The last block is for the one person you did not spend the evening with. Our [interactive Halloween card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) is built for that, not for parties. You add their name, a letter, up to six photos and a word to carve; they knock three times, carve a jack-o'-lantern until your word glows and read your letter by flashlight.

It ends with "Will you be my boo?" and a Boo License, with modes for a partner, best friend, family or kids. Platform-wide, not Halloween data, 90.9% of started pages are published and each averages 11.1 views.

If you will be asleep or working at midnight, the [premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) has an optional unlock time. Until then the link shows only their name and a countdown, so you can send it at 7 pm and have it open at 12.

## When this plan, or a midnight card, is the wrong choice

A timetable is wrong for a toddler who is done by 5:40 pm; follow the child. It is also wrong if your town moves trick-or-treat off a Sunday Halloween, as in 2027.

A card loses to a knock on the door when the person is in the same building, and to a phone call for a grandparent without a smartphone. The interface is English only, and since only 48.3% of opens are on a phone, test it on a laptop too.

## Sources

- CDC, MMWR, Halloween child pedestrian deaths 1975–1996, 24 October 1997.
- Hsu et al., IJERPH, UK Halloween child traffic injuries, 2021 (abstract read).
- Leung et al., CMAJ, holiday nut anaphylaxis in Canadian children, 2020 (abstract read).
- Joel Best, "Halloween Sadism: The Evidence" (undated).
- FARE, Teal Pumpkin Project (undated).

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine has a reason to cite this over today.com and the weak pages below it: it is the only result that turns 31 October into an hour-by-hour plan by persona with cost and indoor/outdoor per idea, and the only one with sourced safety (CDC and UK crash hours, Joel Best on the poisoned-candy myth, CMAJ nut anaphylaxis). The SERP is mostly spam, which helps, but today.com's domain authority and 59-item breadth will outrank a new low-authority page for the head phrasing; the first-party data is platform-wide, not Halloween-specific, so the moat is the structure and sourcing rather than unique numbers.
